<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:18pt;margin-left:4.54%;text-indent:0%;font-style:italic;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Convertible Senior Notes and Capped Call Transactions &#8211; Impact on Earnings per Share</p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-size:6pt;">&#160;</p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:4.54%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">The <ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_xbrlishares" id="F_001138" name="us-gaap:AntidilutiveSecuritiesExcludedFromComputationOfEarningsPerShareAmount" contextRef="C_0001439404_us-gaapDerivativeInstrumentRiskAxis_zngaConvertibleSeniorNotesDueTwoZeroTwoSixMember_us-gaapStatementClassOfStockAxis_us-gaapCommonClassAMember_20200101_20201231" decimals="-5" scale="6">66.9</ix:nonFraction> million shares initially underlying the conversion option of the 2026 Notes and the <ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_xbrlishares" id="F_001137" name="us-gaap:AntidilutiveSecuritiesExcludedFromComputationOfEarningsPerShareAmount" contextRef="C_0001439404_us-gaapDerivativeInstrumentRiskAxis_zngaConvertibleSeniorNotesAndCappedCallTransactionsMember_us-gaapStatementClassOfStockAxis_us-gaapCommonClassAMember_20200101_20201231" decimals="-5" scale="6">83.1</ix:nonFraction> million shares initially underlying the conversion option of the 2024 Notes will not have an impact on our diluted earnings per share until the Company has a period of net income and the average market price of our Class&#160;A common stock exceeds the respective conversion price of the 2026 Notes and 2024 Notes, as we intend and have the ability to settle the principal amount of the 2026 Notes and 2024 Notes in cash upon conversion. The Company computes the potentially dilutive impact of the shares of Class&#160;A common stock related to the 2026 Notes and 2024 Notes using the treasury stock method. The 2026 Capped Calls and 2024 Capped Calls are excluded from the calculation of diluted earnings per share, as they would be antidilutive under the treasury stock method.</p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;">&#160;</p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:8pt;margin-left:4.54%;text-indent:0%;font-style:italic;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Credit Facility</p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:6pt;text-indent:4.54%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">In December 2020, the Company entered into a credit agreement (the &#8220;2020 Credit Agreement&#8221;) with certain financial institutions that provides for a <span style="-sec-ix-hidden:F_001139">three-year</span> revolving credit facility in an aggregate principal amount of up to $<ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD" id="F_001140" name="us-gaap:LineOfCreditFacilityMaximumBorrowingCapacity" contextRef="C_0001439404_us-gaapCreditFacilityAxis_us-gaapRevolvingCreditFacilityMember_us-gaapLineOfCreditFacilityAxis_zngaBankOfAmericaNAMember_20201231" decimals="-5" scale="6">425.0</ix:nonFraction> million and is secured by a blanket lien on the Company&#8217;s assets. The Company may borrow, repay and re-borrow funds under the Credit Agreement until December 31, 2023, at which time the 2020 Credit Agreement will terminate, and all outstanding revolving loans, together with all accrued and unpaid interest, must be repaid. The Company may use the proceeds of future borrowings under the 2020 Credit Agreement for general corporate purposes.</p>

<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;;font-size:9pt;">&#160;</p></ix:nonNumeric><ix:nonNumeric id="F_000383" name="us-gaap:ShareholdersEquityAndShareBasedPaymentsTextBlock" contextRef="C_0001439404_20200101_20201231" escape="true" continuedAt="F_000383_dcnt_41cf7821-d442-4455-a04f-091d317bf507">
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;">&#160;</p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">12. Stockholders&#8217; Equity and Other Employee Benefits</p>
<p style="margin-top:6pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:4.54%;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Common Stock</p>
<p style="margin-top:6pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:4.54%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;"><ix:nonNumeric id="F_001184" name="us-gaap:ConversionOfStockDescription" contextRef="C_0001439404_20180501_20180502">Our three classes of common stock are Class&#160;A, Class B and Class C common stock. On May 2, 2018, our founder, Mark Pincus, elected to convert certain outstanding shares of Class B common stock and all outstanding shares of Class C common stock controlled by Mr. Pincus and an affiliated investment entity into an equivalent number of shares of Class A common stock. As a result of Mr. Pincus&#8217; conversion, the remaining shares of Class B common stock represented less than <ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_xbrlipure" id="F_001185" name="znga:MaximumPercentageOfCommonStockOutstandingRequiredForConversion" contextRef="C_0001439404_us-gaapStatementClassOfStockAxis_us-gaapCommonClassBMember_20180501_20180502" decimals="INF" scale="-2">10</ix:nonFraction>% of the total voting power of all Zynga stockholders and, accordingly, each remaining outstanding share of Class B common stock automatically converted into <ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_xbrlishares" id="F_001186" name="us-gaap:ConversionOfStockSharesIssued1" contextRef="C_0001439404_us-gaapStatementClassOfStockAxis_us-gaapCommonClassAMember_20180501_20180502" decimals="INF" format="ixt-sec:numwordsen">one</ix:nonFraction> share of Class A common stock. Each Zynga stockholder now has <ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_zngaVoting_Rights" id="F_001187" name="znga:NumberOfVotingRights" contextRef="C_0001439404_20180502" decimals="INF" format="ixt-sec:numwordsen">one</ix:nonFraction> vote per share on all matters subject to stockholder vote. Following the conversion, <ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_xbrlishares" id="F_001188" name="us-gaap:CommonStockSharesOutstanding" contextRef="C_0001439404_us-gaapStatementClassOfStockAxis_us-gaapCommonClassBMember_20180502" decimals="INF" format="ixt-sec:numwordsen"><ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_xbrlishares" id="F_001189" name="us-gaap:CommonStockSharesOutstanding" contextRef="C_0001439404_us-gaapStatementClassOfStockAxis_us-gaapCommonClassCMember_20180502" decimals="INF" format="ixt-sec:numwordsen">no</ix:nonFraction></ix:nonFraction> shares of Class B or Class C common stock are outstanding.</ix:nonNumeric> </p>
<p style="margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:4.54%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">The following are the rights and privileges of our classes of common stock:</p>
<p style="margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:4.54%;font-style:italic;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Dividends.<span style="font-style:normal;"> The holders of outstanding shares of our common stock are entitled to receive dividends out of funds legally available at the times and in the amounts which our Board of Directors may determine.</span></p><ix:nonNumeric id="F_001190" name="us-gaap:CommonStockVotingRights" contextRef="C_0001439404_20200101_20201231"><p style="margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:4.54%;font-style:italic;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Voting Rights.<span style="font-style:normal;"> Holders of our Class&#160;A common stock are entitled to <ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_zngaVoting_Rights" id="F_001191" name="znga:NumberOfVotingRights" contextRef="C_0001439404_us-gaapStatementClassOfStockAxis_us-gaapCommonClassAMember_20201231" decimals="INF" format="ixt-sec:numwordsen">one</ix:nonFraction> vote per share.</span></p></ix:nonNumeric>
<p style="margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:4.54%;font-style:italic;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Liquidation.<span style="font-style:normal;"> Upon our liquidation, dissolution or winding-up, the assets legally available for distribution to our stockholders would be distributable ratably among the holders of our Class&#160;A common stock.</span></p>
<p style="margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:4.54%;font-style:italic;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Preemptive or Similar Rights.<span style="font-style:normal;"> None of our common stock is entitled to preemptive rights or subject to redemption.</span></p><ix:nonNumeric id="F_001192" name="us-gaap:ConversionOfStockDescription" contextRef="C_0001439404_20200101_20201231" continuedAt="F_001192_dcnt_082bb586-95d6-4794-90d2-5b5e790a4607"><p style="margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:4.54%;font-style:italic;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Conversion.<span style="font-style:normal;"> Our Class&#160;A common stock is not convertible into any other shares of our capital stock. The Class&#160;B and Class C common stock converted into Class A common stock may not be reissued.</span></p>
</ix:nonNumeric></ix:nonNumeric><p style="text-align:center;margin-top:12pt;margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">91</p>
<hr style="page-break-after:always" /><ix:continuation id="F_000383_dcnt_41cf7821-d442-4455-a04f-091d317bf507" continuedAt="F_000383_dcnt_e8afb863-54cf-48c9-b42b-eeb699eb71ce"><ix:continuation id="F_001192_dcnt_082bb586-95d6-4794-90d2-5b5e790a4607">
</ix:continuation>
<p style="margin-top:18pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:4.54%;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Stock Repurchases</p>
<p style="margin-top:6pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:4.54%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">In April 2018, a share repurchase program was authorized for up to $<ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD" id="F_001193" name="us-gaap:StockRepurchaseProgramAuthorizedAmount1" contextRef="C_0001439404_srtRangeAxis_srtMaximumMember_us-gaapShareRepurchaseProgramAxis_zngaTwoThousandAndEighteenShareRepurchaseProgramMember_us-gaapStatementClassOfStockAxis_us-gaapCommonClassAMember_20180430" decimals="INF" scale="6">200.0</ix:nonFraction> million of our outstanding Class A common stock (the &#8220;2018 Share Repurchase Program&#8221;). The timing and amount of any stock repurchase will be determined based on market conditions, share price and other factors. The program does not require us to repurchase any specific number of shares of our Class A common stock and may be modified, suspended or terminated at any time without notice. The 2018 Share Repurchase Program is authorized to remain in effect until April 2022 and will be funded from existing cash on hand or other sources of funding as the Company may determine to be appropriate. Share repurchases under these authorizations may be made through a variety of methods, which may include open market purchases, privately negotiated transactions, block trades, accelerated share repurchase transactions, purchases through 10b5-1 plans or by any combination of such methods. </p>
<p style="margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:4.54%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">As of December&#160;31, 2020, we had $<ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD" id="F_001194" name="us-gaap:PaymentsForRepurchaseOfCommonStock" contextRef="C_0001439404_us-gaapShareRepurchaseProgramAxis_zngaTwoThousandAndEighteenShareRepurchaseProgramMember_20200101_20201231" decimals="-5" scale="6">173.8</ix:nonFraction> million remaining under the 2018 Share Repurchase Program. The 2018 Share Repurchase Program is authorized to remain in effect until <span style="-sec-ix-hidden:F_001195">April 2022</span>.</p>
<p style="margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:4.54%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">All of our stock repurchases were made through open market purchases under Rule 10b5-1 plans and subsequently retired.</p>
<p style="margin-top:18pt;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:4.54%;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Equity Incentive Plans and Stock-Based Compensation Expense</p>
<p style="margin-top:6pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:4.54%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">In 2007, we adopted the 2007 Equity Incentive Plan (the &#8220;2007 Plan&#8221;) for the purpose of granting stock options and RSUs to employees, directors and non-employees. Concurrent with the effectiveness of our initial public offering on December&#160;15, 2011, we adopted the 2011 Equity Incentive Plan (the &#8220;2011 Plan&#8221;), and all remaining common shares reserved for future grant or issuance under the 2007 Plan were added to the 2011 Plan. The 2011 Plan was adopted for purposes of granting stock options and RSUs to employees, directors and non-employees. <ix:nonNumeric id="F_001196" name="us-gaap:EmployeeStockOwnershipPlanESOPMethodOfMeasuringCompensation" contextRef="C_0001439404_20200101_20201231">The number of shares of our Class&#160;A common stock reserved for future issuance under our 2011 Plan will automatically increase on January&#160;1 of each year, beginning on January&#160;1, 2012, and continuing through and including January&#160;1, 2021, by <ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_xbrlipure" id="F_001197" name="znga:AnnualIncreaseAsPercentageOfCommonStockSharesOutstanding" contextRef="C_0001439404_us-gaapStatementClassOfStockAxis_us-gaapCommonClassAMember_20200101_20201231" decimals="2" scale="-2">4</ix:nonFraction>% of the total number of shares of our capital stock outstanding as of December&#160;31 of the preceding calendar year or such lesser number of shares that may be determined by the Company&#8217;s Board of Directors. During the year ended December 31, 2020, there was <ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_xbrlishares" id="F_001198" name="znga:CommonStockCapitalSharesReservedForFutureIssuanceIncreases" contextRef="C_0001439404_us-gaapStatementClassOfStockAxis_us-gaapCommonClassAMember_20200101_20201231" decimals="INF" format="ixt-sec:numwordsen">no</ix:nonFraction> increase in the Class A common stock reserved for future issuance under the 2011 Plan. </ix:nonNumeric></p><ix:nonNumeric id="F_000446_2" name="us-gaap:ScheduleOfEmployeeServiceShareBasedCompensationAllocationOfRecognizedPeriodCostsTextBlock" contextRef="C_0001439404_20200101_20201231" escape="true"><ix:nonNumeric id="F_000446" name="us-gaap:ScheduleOfEmployeeServiceShareBasedCompensationAllocationOfRecognizedPeriodCostsTextBlock" contextRef="C_0001439404_20200101_20201231" escape="true">

<p style="margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:4.54%;font-style:italic;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Performance RSU</p>
<p style="margin-top:6pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:4.54%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">On March 15, 2020, the Company granted performance-based awards to certain executive officers (the &#8220;Executive Officer Performance RSUs&#8221;). <ix:nonNumeric id="F_001279" name="us-gaap:ConversionOfStockDescription" contextRef="C_0001439404_us-gaapAwardTypeAxis_zngaPerformanceRSUsMember_20200315_20200315">The number of shares earned ranged from <ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_xbrlipure" id="F_001280" name="znga:NumberOfAwardsEarnedPercentage" contextRef="C_0001439404_srtRangeAxis_srtMinimumMember_us-gaapAwardTypeAxis_zngaPerformanceRSUsMember_20200315_20200315" decimals="INF" scale="-2">0</ix:nonFraction>% to <ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_xbrlipure" id="F_001281" name="znga:NumberOfAwardsEarnedPercentage" contextRef="C_0001439404_srtRangeAxis_srtMaximumMember_us-gaapAwardTypeAxis_zngaPerformanceRSUsMember_20200315_20200315" decimals="INF" scale="-2">120</ix:nonFraction>% of the target number of shares granted and were dependent upon on actual operating cash flows for the year ended December 31, 2020 relative to pre-established thresholds. The target number of shares granted totaled <ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD" id="F_001282" name="us-gaap:DelinquentAmountAtEndOfPeriodOnLoansManagedAndSecuritized" contextRef="C_0001439404_us-gaapAwardTypeAxis_zngaPerformanceRSUsMember_20200315" decimals="-5" scale="6">0.6</ix:nonFraction> million and based on actual operating cash flows for the year ended December 31, 2020, the highest threshold was achieved resulting in the actual shares earned of <ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD" id="F_001283" name="znga:SharesEarned" contextRef="C_0001439404_20200315" decimals="-5" scale="6">0.7</ix:nonFraction> million. The shares earned will vest over a period of four years following the grant date, with <ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_xbrlipure" id="F_001284" name="us-gaap:SharebasedCompensationArrangementBySharebasedPaymentAwardAwardVestingRightsPercentage" contextRef="C_0001439404_us-gaapAwardTypeAxis_zngaPerformanceRSUsMember_20200315_20200315" decimals="INF" scale="-2">25</ix:nonFraction>% vesting on the one year anniversary of the grant date and the remaining quarterly thereafter, subject to continued service by the executives.</ix:nonNumeric> </p>
<p style="margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:4.54%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Outside of the Executive Officer Performance PSUs, certain employees are eligible to receive Performance RSUs, which are subject to performance and time-based vesting requirements. The target number of shares of the Performance RSUs are adjusted based on our business performance measured against the performance goals approved by the Compensation Committee at the date of employment with the Company. <ix:nonNumeric id="F_001288" name="us-gaap:ShareBasedCompensationArrangementByShareBasedPaymentAwardAwardVestingRights" contextRef="C_0001439404_srtTitleOfIndividualAxis_zngaEmployeeMember_us-gaapAwardTypeAxis_us-gaapPerformanceSharesMember_20200101_20201231">Generally, if the performance criteria are satisfied, 25% of the award will vest immediately or soon after with the remaining vesting ratably for each quarter or six month periods thereafter.</ix:nonNumeric> </p>
<p style="margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:4.54%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">During the years ended December 31, 2020, 2019 and 2018, we recorded $<ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD" id="F_001285" name="us-gaap:AllocatedShareBasedCompensationExpense" contextRef="C_0001439404_srtTitleOfIndividualAxis_zngaEmployeeMember_us-gaapAwardTypeAxis_us-gaapPerformanceSharesMember_20200101_20201231" decimals="-5" scale="6">2.8</ix:nonFraction> million, $<ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD" id="F_001286" name="us-gaap:AllocatedShareBasedCompensationExpense" contextRef="C_0001439404_srtTitleOfIndividualAxis_zngaEmployeeMember_us-gaapAwardTypeAxis_us-gaapPerformanceSharesMember_20190101_20191231" decimals="-5" scale="6">1.2</ix:nonFraction> million and $<ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD" id="F_001287" name="us-gaap:AllocatedShareBasedCompensationExpense" contextRef="C_0001439404_srtTitleOfIndividualAxis_zngaEmployeeMember_us-gaapAwardTypeAxis_us-gaapPerformanceSharesMember_20180101_20181231" decimals="-5" scale="6">1.8</ix:nonFraction> million, respectively, of stock-based compensation expense related to Performance RSUs. </p>
<p style="margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:4.54%;font-style:italic;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Market RSUs</p>
<p style="margin-top:6pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:4.54%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">On March 15, 2020, the Company granted Market RSUs to certain executive officers, with two separate prescribed measurement periods. Both prescribed measurement periods began on the grant date, with the first prescribed measurement period ending on December 31, 2021 (the &#8220;Two-Year Market RSUs&#8221;) and the second period ending on December 31, 2022 (the &#8220;Three-Year Market RSUs&#8221;). The number of RSUs earned (if any) will range from <ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_xbrlipure" id="F_001289" name="znga:NumberOfAwardsEarnedPercentage" contextRef="C_0001439404_srtRangeAxis_srtMinimumMember_us-gaapAwardTypeAxis_zngaMarketConditionRSUsMember_us-gaapExtinguishmentOfDebtAxis_zngaLongTermInvestmentsMember_20200315_20200315" decimals="INF" scale="-2">0</ix:nonFraction>% to <ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_xbrlipure" id="F_001290" name="znga:NumberOfAwardsEarnedPercentage" contextRef="C_0001439404_srtRangeAxis_srtMaximumMember_us-gaapAwardTypeAxis_zngaMarketConditionRSUsMember_us-gaapExtinguishmentOfDebtAxis_zngaLongTermInvestmentsMember_20200315_20200315" decimals="INF" scale="-2">150</ix:nonFraction>% of the target number of shares, depending on actual achievement of specific tiers for Zynga&#8217;s total shareholder return (&#8220;TSR&#8221;) relative to the TSR of companies comprising the S&#38;P MidCap 400 Index over the prescribed measurement periods. If Zynga&#8217;s TSR is negative during any measurement period, the number of RSUs earned is capped at <ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_xbrlipure" id="F_001291" name="us-gaap:ShareBasedCompensationArrangementByShareBasedPaymentAwardFairValueAssumptionsExpectedVolatilityRate" contextRef="C_0001439404_us-gaapAwardTypeAxis_zngaMarketConditionRSUsMember_20200315_20200315" decimals="INF" scale="-2">100</ix:nonFraction>% of the target number of shares for that prescribed measurement period.</p>
<p style="margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:4.54%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Any shares earned will vest in three equal annual increments, beginning on March 15 of the year following the conclusion of each prescribed measurement period, subject to continued service by the executives. The target number of shares totaled <ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD" id="F_001292" name="us-gaap:DelinquentAmountAtEndOfPeriodOnLoansManagedAndSecuritized" contextRef="C_0001439404_us-gaapAwardTypeAxis_zngaTwoYearMarketRSUsMember_us-gaapExtinguishmentOfDebtAxis_zngaLongTermAwardsMember_20200315" decimals="-5" scale="6">2.2</ix:nonFraction> million each for the Two-Year Market RSUs and the Three-Year Market RSUs, for a total of <ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD" id="F_001293" name="us-gaap:DelinquentAmountAtEndOfPeriodOnLoansManagedAndSecuritized" contextRef="C_0001439404_us-gaapAwardTypeAxis_zngaThreeYearMarketRSUsMember_us-gaapExtinguishmentOfDebtAxis_zngaLongTermAwardsMember_20200315" decimals="-5" scale="6">4.4</ix:nonFraction> million target shares.</p>
<p style="margin-top:18pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:4.54%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">The estimated per share grant date fair value of the Two-Year Market RSUs and Three-Year Market RSUs was $<ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD_xbrlishares" id="F_001294" name="us-gaap:SharebasedCompensationArrangementBySharebasedPaymentAwardOptionsVestedWeightedAverageGrantDateFairValue" contextRef="C_0001439404_us-gaapAwardTypeAxis_zngaTwoYearMarketRSUsMember_us-gaapExtinguishmentOfDebtAxis_zngaLongTermAwardsMember_20200315_20200315" decimals="2">7.37</ix:nonFraction> and $<ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD_xbrlishares" id="F_001295" name="us-gaap:SharebasedCompensationArrangementBySharebasedPaymentAwardOptionsVestedWeightedAverageGrantDateFairValue" contextRef="C_0001439404_us-gaapAwardTypeAxis_zngaThreeYearMarketRSUsMember_us-gaapExtinguishmentOfDebtAxis_zngaLongTermAwardsMember_20200315_20200315" decimals="2">7.41</ix:nonFraction>, respectively. The significant assumptions used in estimating the grant date fair value of each award include an expected volatility of 27%, a risk-free interest rate ranging from <ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_xbrlipure" id="F_001296" name="us-gaap:ShareBasedCompensationArrangementByShareBasedPaymentAwardFairValueAssumptionsRiskFreeInterestRate" contextRef="C_0001439404_srtRangeAxis_srtMinimumMember_us-gaapExtinguishmentOfDebtAxis_zngaLongTermAwardsMember_20200315_20200315" decimals="3" scale="-2">0.5</ix:nonFraction>% to <ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_xbrlipure" id="F_001297" name="us-gaap:ShareBasedCompensationArrangementByShareBasedPaymentAwardFairValueAssumptionsRiskFreeInterestRate" contextRef="C_0001439404_srtRangeAxis_srtMaximumMember_us-gaapExtinguishmentOfDebtAxis_zngaLongTermAwardsMember_20200315_20200315" decimals="3" scale="-2">0.6</ix:nonFraction>% and an expected dividend yield of zero. During the year ended December 31, 2020, we recorded $<ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD" id="F_001298" name="us-gaap:AllocatedShareBasedCompensationExpense" contextRef="C_0001439404_us-gaapAwardTypeAxis_zngaMarketConditionRSUsMember_20200315_20200315" decimals="-5" scale="6">8.0</ix:nonFraction> million of stock-based compensation expense related to the Market RSUs. </p>
<p style="margin-top:18pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:4.54%;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">2011 Employee Stock Purchase Plan</p>
<p style="margin-top:6pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:4.54%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Our 2011 Employee Stock Purchase Plan (&#8220;2011 ESPP&#8221;), was approved by our Board of Directors in September 2011 and by our stockholders in November 2011 and amended in August 2012. The number of shares of our Class&#160;A common stock reserved for future issuance under our 2011 ESPP will automatically increase on January&#160;1 of each year, beginning on January&#160;1, 2012, and continuing through and including January&#160;1, 2021, by the lesser of <ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_xbrlipure" id="F_001299" name="znga:PercentageOfCapitalStockOutstanding" contextRef="C_0001439404_us-gaapPlanNameAxis_zngaTwoThousandElevenESPPMember_us-gaapStatementClassOfStockAxis_us-gaapCommonClassAMember_20111128_20111130" decimals="INF" scale="-2">2</ix:nonFraction>% of the total number of shares of our capital stock outstanding as of December&#160;31 of the preceding calendar year, <ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_xbrlishares" id="F_001300" name="znga:CommonStockCapitalSharesReservedForFutureIssuanceIncreases" contextRef="C_0001439404_us-gaapPlanNameAxis_zngaTwoThousandElevenESPPMember_us-gaapStatementClassOfStockAxis_us-gaapCommonClassAMember_20111128_20111130" decimals="INF" format="ixt:numdotdecimal">25,000,000</ix:nonFraction> shares or the number of shares that may be determined by the Company&#8217;s Board of Directors. During the year ended December 31, 2020, there was <ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_xbrlishares" id="F_001301" name="znga:CommonStockCapitalSharesReservedForFutureIssuanceIncreases" contextRef="C_0001439404_us-gaapPlanNameAxis_zngaTwoThousandElevenESPPMember_us-gaapStatementClassOfStockAxis_us-gaapCommonClassAMember_20200101_20201231" decimals="INF" format="ixt-sec:numwordsen">no</ix:nonFraction> increase in the Class A common stock reserved for future issuance under the 2011 ESPP.</p>
<p style="margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:4.54%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Our 2011 ESPP permits participants to purchase shares of our Class&#160;A common stock through payroll deductions up to <ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_xbrlipure" id="F_001303" name="us-gaap:ShareBasedCompensationArrangementByShareBasedPaymentAwardMaximumEmployeeSubscriptionRate" contextRef="C_0001439404_us-gaapPlanNameAxis_zngaTwoThousandElevenESPPMember_us-gaapStatementClassOfStockAxis_us-gaapCommonClassAMember_20111130" decimals="INF" scale="-2">15</ix:nonFraction>% of their earnings, subject to a maximum of <ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_xbrlishares" id="F_001302" name="us-gaap:ShareBasedCompensationArrangementByShareBasedPaymentAwardMaximumNumberOfSharesPerEmployee" contextRef="C_0001439404_us-gaapPlanNameAxis_zngaTwoThousandElevenESPPMember_us-gaapStatementClassOfStockAxis_us-gaapCommonClassAMember_20111128_20111130" decimals="INF" format="ixt:numdotdecimal">5,000</ix:nonFraction> shares available for purchase on any purchase date. Unless otherwise determined by the administrator, the purchase price of the shares will be <ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_xbrlipure" id="F_001304" name="znga:ShareBasedCompensationArrangementByShareBasedPaymentAwardEmployeeDiscountRate" contextRef="C_0001439404_us-gaapPlanNameAxis_zngaTwoThousandElevenESPPMember_us-gaapStatementClassOfStockAxis_us-gaapCommonClassAMember_20111130" decimals="2" scale="-2">85</ix:nonFraction>% of the lower of the fair market value of our Class&#160;A common stock on the first day of an offering or on the date of purchase. The ESPP offers two purchase dates within each annual period, resulting in a six-month and twelve-month look-back. Additionally, the ESPP contains an automatic reset feature after the first six months of each annual period, such that if the fair market value of our Class A common stock has decreased from the original offering date, the offering will automatically terminate and all participants will be re-enrolled in the new, lower-priced offering for the remaining six months.&#160;&#160;Participants may end their participation at any time during an offering and will be refunded their accrued contributions that have not yet been used to purchase shares. Participation ends automatically upon termination of employment.</p>

<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-size:8pt;">&#160;</p><ix:nonNumeric id="F_000385" name="us-gaap:EarningsPerShareTextBlock" contextRef="C_0001439404_20200101_20201231" escape="true" continuedAt="F_000385_dcnt_e256950a-90bd-4a4b-ba0c-68ca190b2cf8">
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">14. Net Income (Loss) Per Share of Common Stock</p><ix:nonNumeric id="F_000414" name="us-gaap:EarningsPerSharePolicyTextBlock" contextRef="C_0001439404_20200101_20201231" escape="true" continuedAt="F_000414_dcnt_41cca464-b3cb-4d2e-b196-ba90fe8417d3">
<p style="margin-top:6pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:4.54%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;"><ix:nonNumeric id="F_001350" name="us-gaap:ConversionOfStockDescription" contextRef="C_0001439404_us-gaapStatementClassOfStockAxis_zngaClassABAndCCommonStockMember_20200101_20201231">As noted previously, our founder, Mark Pincus, elected to convert certain outstanding shares of Class B common stock and all outstanding shares of Class C common stock controlled by Mr. Pincus and an affiliated investment entity into an equivalent number of shares of Class A common stock in May 2018. Following the conversion, <ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_xbrlishares" id="F_001351" name="us-gaap:CommonStockSharesOutstanding" contextRef="C_0001439404_us-gaapStatementClassOfStockAxis_us-gaapCommonClassBMember_20180502" decimals="INF" format="ixt-sec:numwordsen"><ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_xbrlishares" id="F_001352" name="us-gaap:CommonStockSharesOutstanding" contextRef="C_0001439404_us-gaapStatementClassOfStockAxis_us-gaapCommonClassCMember_20180502" decimals="INF" format="ixt-sec:numwordsen">no</ix:nonFraction></ix:nonFraction> shares of Class B or Class C common stock are outstanding and accordingly, the Company calculated basic and dilutive net income (loss) per share under a single-class method</ix:nonNumeric>.&#160;&#160;</p>
<p style="margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:4.54%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Basic net income (loss) per share is computed by dividing net income (loss) attributable to common stockholders by the weighted-average number of common shares outstanding during the period. Diluted net income (loss) per share is computed by dividing net income (loss) attributable to common stockholders by the weighted-average number of common shares outstanding, including potential dilutive securities. In computing diluted net income (loss) per share, net income (loss) attributable to common shareholders is re-allocated to reflect the potential impact of dilutive securities, including stock options, unvested RSUs, unvested performance and market-based RSUs, ESPP withholdings and convertible debt instruments. For periods in which we have generated a </p>
</ix:nonNumeric></ix:nonNumeric><p style="text-align:center;margin-top:12pt;margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">95</p>
<hr style="page-break-after:always" /><ix:continuation id="F_000385_dcnt_e256950a-90bd-4a4b-ba0c-68ca190b2cf8"><ix:continuation id="F_000414_dcnt_41cca464-b3cb-4d2e-b196-ba90fe8417d3">
<p style="margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;"><span style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">net loss or there is no income attributable to common stockholders, we do not include dilutive securities in our calculation of diluted net income (loss) per share, as the impact of these awards is anti-dilutive. </span></p></ix:continuation><ix:nonNumeric id="F_000452" name="us-gaap:ScheduleOfEarningsPerShareBasicAndDilutedTableTextBlock" contextRef="C_0001439404_20200101_20201231" escape="true">

<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;">&#160;</p>
<p style="margin-top:2pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:4.54%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Excluded from tables above is our uncertain income tax position liability of $<ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD" id="F_001396" name="us-gaap:UnrecognizedTaxBenefitsIncomeTaxPenaltiesAndInterestAccrued" contextRef="C_0001439404_20201231" decimals="-5" scale="6">24.8</ix:nonFraction> million, which includes interest and penalties, as the Company cannot make a reasonably reliable estimate of the period of cash settlement. </p><ix:nonNumeric id="F_000415" name="znga:LegalContingenciesPolicyTextBlock" contextRef="C_0001439404_20200101_20201231" escape="true">
<p style="margin-top:18pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:4.54%;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Legal Matters</p></ix:nonNumeric>
<p style="margin-top:6pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:4.54%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">The Company is involved in legal and regulatory proceedings on an ongoing basis. Some of these proceedings are in early stages and may seek an indeterminate amount of damages. If the Company believes that a loss arising from such matters is probable and can be reasonably estimated, the Company accrues the estimated liability in its financial statements. If only a range of estimated losses can be determined, the Company accrues an amount within the range that, in its judgment, reflects the most likely outcome&#59; if none of the estimates within that range is a better estimate than any other amount, the Company accrues the low end of the range. For proceedings in which an unfavorable outcome is reasonably possible but not probable and an estimate of the loss or range of losses arising from the proceeding can be made, the Company discloses such an estimate, if material. If such a loss or range of losses is not reasonably estimable, the Company discloses that fact. In assessing the materiality of a proceeding, the Company evaluates, among other factors, the amount of monetary damages claimed, as well as the potential impact of non-monetary remedies sought by plaintiffs that may require changes to business practices in a manner that could have a material adverse impact on the Company&#8217;s business.<span style="color:#000000;">&#160;<ix:nonNumeric id="F_000416" name="us-gaap:LegalCostsPolicyTextBlock" contextRef="C_0001439404_20200101_20201231" escape="true">Legal expenses are recognized as incurred.</ix:nonNumeric></span></p>
<p style="margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:4.54%;color:#000000;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">On September 12, 2019, the Company announced that an incident had occurred that may have involved player data (the &#8220;Data Incident&#8221;). Upon our discovery of the Data Incident, an investigation immediately commenced and advisors and third-party forensics firms were retained to assist. The investigation revealed that, during the third quarter of 2019, outside hackers illegally accessed certain player account information and other Zynga information, and that no financial information was accessed. The Company has provided notifications to players, investors, regulators and other third parties, where we believe notice was required or appropriate. <span style="color:#000000;">The Company has exchanged correspondence with certain regulators as a result of the incident. The Company has also received and has responded to data subject access requests from certain European Union players of Zynga&#8217;s games.</span></p>
<p style="margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:4.54%;color:#000000;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Since March 3, 2020, five consumer class action complaints have been filed in connection with the Data Incident in federal court. On <span style="color:#000000;">March 3, 2020, two plaintiffs &#8211; minor &#8220;I.C.&#8221; (acting through his parent Nasim Chaudhri) and Amy Gitre &#8211; filed a class action complaint arising out of the Data Incident (the &#8220;</span><span style="font-style:italic;color:#000000;">Chaudhri</span><span style="color:#000000;"> complaint&#8221;), generally alleging that Zynga failed to reasonably safeguard certain player information, including names, email addresses, and passwords (among other items)&#59; failed to provide them with timely notification of the breach&#59; and made misleading representations concerning the safety and security of plaintiffs&#8217; personal information. Plaintiffs allege claims against Zynga under several state law theories, including negligence, intrusion upon seclusion, failure to comply with data breach notification statutes, and unjust enrichment, and they seek injunctive relief and damages. Zynga filed a motion to compel arbitration and arbitration-related discovery on May 8, 2020. </span></p>
<p style="margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:4.54%;color:#000000;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">On <span style="color:#000000;">March 23, 2020, plaintiffs Carol Johnson and Lisa Thomas filed a second class action complaint in the Northern District of California federal court (the &#8220;</span><span style="font-style:italic;color:#000000;">Johnson</span><span style="color:#000000;"> complaint&#8221;). Similar to the </span><span style="font-style:italic;color:#000000;">Chaudhri</span><span style="color:#000000;"> complaint, the </span><span style="font-style:italic;color:#000000;">Johnson</span><span style="color:#000000;"> plaintiffs &#8211; residents of Missouri and Wisconsin &#8211; assert Zynga failed to adequately protect certain player information, including names, email addresses, and passwords (among other items). Plaintiffs contend that, despite Zynga&#8217;s representations in its privacy policy that sensitive player information would be adequately protected, plaintiffs&#8217; passwords were stored using inadequate hashing methods or in plain text. Plaintiffs allege that the lack of adequate security measures caused them harm as a result of the Data Incident, and they assert numerous various claims against Zynga, including claims for negligence, negligence per se, unjust enrichment, declaratory relief, breach of confidence, breach of contract and implied contract, violations of California&#8217;s Unfair Competition Law (&#8220;UCL&#8221;, CGL 17200, et seq.), and state-specific violations of Missouri&#8217;s Merchandising Practices Act and Wisconsin&#8217;s Deceptive Trade Practices Act.&#160;Plaintiffs seek damages, as well as declaratory and injunctive relief. On May 26, 2020, Zynga filed a motion to compel arbitration and arbitration-related discovery.</span></p>
<p style="margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:4.54%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">On April 15, 2020, plaintiffs Joseph Martinez IV and Daniel Petro, residents of Colorado and Iowa, filed a third class action complaint in the Northern District of California (the &#8220;<span style="font-style:italic;">Martinez</span> complaint&#8221;). Plaintiffs allege they are longtime Zynga players who were affected by the Data Incident. Similar to the <span style="font-style:italic;">Chaudhri</span> and <span style="font-style:italic;">Johnson</span> plaintiffs, the <span style="font-style:italic;">Martinez</span> plaintiffs generally allege that Zynga </p>
</ix:continuation><p style="text-align:center;margin-top:12pt;margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">97</p>
<hr style="page-break-after:always" /><ix:continuation id="F_000386_dcnt_d8f89cc4-4d2d-415f-a441-16c85392a0ab">
<p style="margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;"><span style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">failed to adequately store and protect or otherwise secure </span><span style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">certain player information</span><span style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">, including names, email addresses, </span><span style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">and </span><span style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">passwords</span><span style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;"> (among other items)</span><span style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">&#59; that Zynga </span><span style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">used </span><span style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">outdated and </span><span style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">improper</span><span style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;"> password encryption methods&#59; that Zynga failed to adequately provide notice of the Data Incident&#59; and that they have been harmed as a result of the Data Incident. Like </span><span style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">the </span><span style="font-style:italic;">Johnson </span><span style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">and </span><span style="font-style:italic;">Chaudhri</span><span style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;"> plaintiffs</span><span style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">, the </span><span style="font-style:italic;">Martinez </span><span style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">plaintiffs assert claims for negligence, negligence per se, and unjust enrichment, as well as contractual claims, and claims for relief under multiple state consumer protection statutes.&#160;Additionally, the </span><span style="font-style:italic;">Martinez </span><span style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">plaintiffs also assert misrepresentation and omission claims under California&#8217;s false advertising law and the California Consumer Legal Remedies Act.&#160;Plaintiffs seek injunctive and monetary relief on behalf of a nationwide class. Zynga responded to the </span><span style="font-style:italic;">Martinez</span><span style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;"> complaint </span><span style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">by filing a motion to compel arbitration on </span><span style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">June 19, 2020.</span></p>
<p style="margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:4.54%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">On January 6, 2021, the district court issued an order in all three of the above actions&#8212;<span style="font-style:italic;">Chaudhri</span>, <span style="font-style:italic;">Johnson</span>, and <span style="font-style:italic;">Martinez</span>&#8212;denying Zynga&#8217;s motions to compel arbitration without prejudice, and granting an alternative request for preliminary arbitration-related discovery that Zynga had made in connection with its motions. Plaintiffs were ordered to provide Zynga with plaintiffs&#8217; identifying information so that Zynga could identify each player&#8217;s records on its systems. A status hearing has been set for March 1, 2021.</p>
<p style="margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:4.54%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">On June 9, 2020 plaintiffs James Oeste and Marissa Oeste, both residents of Maryland, filed a fourth class action complaint in the Northern District of Maryland (the &#8220;<span style="font-style:italic;">Oeste</span> complaint&#8221;). Plaintiffs allege they were Zynga players who were affected by the Data Incident. Similar to all the foregoing plaintiffs, the <span style="font-style:italic;">Oeste</span> plaintiffs seek to represent a nationwide class and generally allege that Zynga failed to adequately or reasonably protect certain player information, including names, email addresses, and passwords (among other items)&#59; that Zynga used outdated or improper password hashing methods&#59; that Zynga failed to adequately provide notice of the Data Incident&#59; and that they have been harmed as a result of the Data Incident. The <span style="font-style:italic;">Oeste</span> plaintiffs assert claims for contractual breach, negligence, negligence per se, invasion of privacy, and claims for relief under California consumer protection and unfair competition statutes. Zynga responded to the complaint on August 31, 2020, with a motion to transfer the action to the Northern District of California. The parties are awaiting the court&#8217;s ruling on the motion.</p>
<p style="margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:4.54%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">On August 13, 2020, plaintiff Christopher Rosiak filed a fifth class action in the Northern District of California (the &#8220;<span style="font-style:italic;">Rosiak</span> complaint&#8221;). Plaintiff alleges similar and analogous claims to those in the <span style="font-style:italic;">Martinez</span> (and other) actions, alleging that he suffered harm as a result of Zynga&#8217;s data breach. Plaintiff Rosiak alleges multiple state law claims, including contract-based claims, negligence, and violation of California&#8217;s unfair competition, false advertising, and consumer protection statutes.&#160;&#160;Pursuant to extension orders granted by the Court, Zynga&#8217;s deadline to respond is currently March 8, 2021.</p>
<p style="margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:4.54%;color:#000000;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">The Company intends to defend itself vigorously against all claims asserted. At this time, the Company is unable to reasonably estimate the loss or range of loss, if any, arising from any of the above-referenced matters.</p>
<p style="margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:4.54%;color:#000000;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">The Company is, at various times, also party to various other legal proceedings and claims not previously discussed which arise in the ordinary course of business. In addition, the Company may receive notifications alleging infringement of patent or other intellectual property rights. Adverse results in any such litigation, legal proceedings or claims may include awards of substantial monetary damages, expensive legal fees, costly royalty or licensing agreements, or orders preventing us from offering certain games, features, or services, and may also result in changes in the Company&#8217;s business practices, which could result in additional costs or a loss of revenue and could otherwise harm the Company&#8217;s business. Although the results of such litigation cannot be predicted with certainty, the Company believes that the amount or range of reasonably possible losses related to such pending or threatened litigation will not have a material adverse effect on its business, operating results, cash flows, or financial condition should such litigation be resolved unfavorably.</p></ix:continuation>

<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;" id="ITEM_9_CHANGES_IN_DISAGREEMENTS_WITH_ACC">ITEM 9. CHANGES IN AND DISAGREEMENTS WITH ACCOUNTANTS ON ACCOUNTING AND FINANCIAL DISCLOSURE</p>
<p style="margin-top:6pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;" id="ITEM_9A_CONTROLS_PROCEDURES">ITEM 9A. CONTROLS AND PROCEDURES</p>
<p style="margin-top:6pt;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:4.54%;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Evaluation of Disclosure Controls and Procedures</p>
<p style="margin-top:6pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:4.54%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Our management, with the participation of our Chief Executive Officer and Chief Financial Officer, evaluated the effectiveness of our disclosure controls and procedures as of the end of the period covered by this Annual Report on Form 10-K. The term &#8220;disclosure controls and procedures,&#8221; as defined in Rules 13a-15(e) and 15d-15(e) under the Exchange Act, means controls and other procedures of a company that are designed to ensure that information required to be disclosed by a company in the reports that it files or submits under the Exchange Act is recorded, processed, summarized and reported, within the time periods specified in the SEC rules and forms. Disclosure controls and procedures include, without limitation, controls and procedures designed to ensure that information required to be disclosed by a company in the reports that it files or submits under the Exchange Act is accumulated and communicated to the company&#8217;s management, including its principal executive and principal financial officers, as appropriate to allow timely decisions regarding required disclosure. Based on the evaluation of our disclosure controls and procedures as of December&#160;31, 2020, our Chief Executive Officer and Chief Financial Officer concluded that, as of such date, our disclosure controls and procedures were effective at the reasonable assurance level.</p>
<p style="margin-top:18pt;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:4.54%;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Management&#8217;s Report on Internal Control over Financial Reporting</p>
<p style="margin-top:6pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:4.54%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Our management is responsible for establishing and maintaining adequate internal control over financial reporting, as defined in Rule 13a-15(f) of the Exchange Act. Our management conducted an evaluation of the effectiveness of our internal control over financial reporting based on the framework in <span style="font-style:italic;">Internal Control&#8212;Integrated Framework </span>issued by the Committee of Sponsoring Organizations of the Treadway Commission (2013 Framework). Based on this evaluation, management concluded that our internal control over financial reporting was effective as of December&#160;31, 2020. Management reviewed the results of its assessment with our Audit Committee. The effectiveness of our internal control over financial reporting as of December&#160;31, 2020 has been audited by Ernst&#160;&#38; Young LLP, an independent registered public accounting firm, as stated in its report which is included in Item&#160;8 under the caption &#8220;Report of Independent Registered Public Accounting Firm&#8221; which is incorporated herein by reference.</p>
<p style="margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:4.54%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">We acquired Peak Oyun Yaz&#305;l&#305;m ve Pazarlama Anonim &#350;irketi and Rollic Games Oyun Yaz&#305;l&#305;m ve Pazarlama Anonim &#350;irketi on July 1, 2020 and October 1, 2020, respectively. As permitted by SEC guidance, we excluded certain internal controls over financial reporting related to these entities from our assessment of the effectiveness of internal control over financial reporting as of December 31, 2020. Combined revenue, operating expenses and total assets subject to these entities&#8217; internal control over financial reporting that are excluded from our assessment of the effectiveness of internal control over financial reporting constituted approximately 2%, 7% and 3% of consolidated revenue, operating expenses and total assets, respectively, excluding acquisition method fair value adjustments, as of and for the year ended December 31, 2020.</p>
<p style="margin-top:18pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:4.54%;font-weight:bold;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Changes in Internal Control over Financial Reporting</p>
<p style="margin-top:6pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:4.54%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">There were no changes in our internal control over financial reporting identified in management&#8217;s evaluation pursuant to Rules 13a-15(d) or 15d-15(d) of the Exchange Act during the quarter ended December&#160;31, 2020 that materially affected, or are reasonably likely to materially affect, our internal control over financial reporting.</p>
<p style="margin-top:18pt;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:4.54%;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Limitations on Effectiveness of Controls and Procedures</p>
<p style="margin-top:6pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:4.54%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">In designing and evaluating the disclosure controls and procedures, management recognizes that any controls and procedures, no matter how well designed and operated, can provide only reasonable assurance of achieving the desired control objectives. In addition, the design of disclosure controls and procedures must reflect the fact that there are resource constraints and that management is required to apply judgment in evaluating the benefits of possible controls and procedures relative to their costs.</p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-size:9pt;">&#160;</p>
